workstream.name: ecl v1 — the real interpreter (design/workstream-v1.md)
workstream.unlocks: M6 can implement contract-checked combinators and guarded idiom recognition against a complete, tested kernel registry instead of inventing data-plane behavior while it builds the generic fallback.

problemStatement: The Zig interpreter is a complete calculator through M4, but its data plane is still the M3 walking seam: only scalar + - * / and scalar comparisons exist, `at` accepts one integer list index, and almost every array/dict/string word is undefined. That means the language does not yet implement d.13 leading-axis pervasion, the d.22 numeric regime over leaves, or the closed kernel surface that justifies ecl's K-style performance model. The high-risk part is not merely adding vocabulary: checked arithmetic, CoW buffer stealing, representation parity, ragged recursion, and future cancellation polls must agree on one ownership and failure protocol before M6 can safely recognize quotations into these loops.
solutionSummary: Introduce a kernel facade plus four focused kernel families. First move the existing scalar arithmetic and `at` behind the facade without changing behavior, freeze an owned-operand/result contract, add explicit index-range and chunk-poll seams, and install skipped proof names. Then implement, independently, numeric/pervasion, sequence/shape/search, ordering/grouping, and dict/text behavior; each family owns its words, tests, and allocator-failure sweep. Finish with real-binary acceptance fixtures and a separate SourceHut oracle job that builds the frozen Rust PoC and compares every shared M5 word while leaving normal `zig build test` independent of Cargo.

mergabilityStrategy.featureFlagStrategy: Ungated. ecl is a clean-slate interpreter with no compatibility population or flag service, and each word is installed atomically as a core binding only when its complete implementation and tests land. Patch 1 is behavior-preserving; Patches 2-5 are independently useful vocabulary slices; Patch 6 adds verification only.
mergabilityStrategy.patchOrderingStrategy: Patch 1 establishes the shared facade, ownership/error/poll contract, and skipped proof names. Patches 2, 3, 4, and 5 depend only on Patch 1 and edit disjoint kernel-family files, so they may execute in parallel. Patch 6 depends on all four behavior patches and adds the cross-runtime harness, acceptance fixture, and CI gate.

currentStateAnalysis: Verified on master at 2bf6c56 (clean and synchronized with origin/master). SourceHut job 1859966 is green for toolchain, fmt, Debug tests, ReleaseSafe tests, instrumented Linux TSan, and ZLint --deny-warnings; local `zig build test`, `zig build test -Doptimize=ReleaseFast`, and the frozen PoC's 44 Rust tests are green. The live runtime path is `main.executeSource` -> `Session.runUnit`/`executeParsed` -> `machine.run`/`dispatch` -> an `env.Primitive` installed by `prims.install`. `src/prims.zig` currently binds scalar + - * /, six comparisons, match, and scalar list-only `at`; no other M5 word is bound. The value substrate is ready: `Value` and `Header` are 16 bytes, `HeapKind` already freezes i64/f64/char1/2/4/symbol/generic/dict/reserved-mask, `heap.isUnique` is acquire-ordered, list constructors specialize at construction, dicts carry cached hashes plus an index, and functional updates document their same-header/new-header ownership convention. Current audited core is 6,361/9,500 lines; the machine component is 2,289/2,300, so primitive wrappers must live in the separately budgeted kernel component rather than expanding `prims.zig`. The Rust oracle implements all shared M5 words except `flip`, `reshape`, and `group`; it stays frozen and is suitable for CLI-level semantic comparison, not as an implementation template for leaves or dispatch.

operationalConsiderations.externalSystemAccess: No runtime external system is added. Patch 6 adds Alpine's packaged Cargo/Rust toolchain to the SourceHut build image solely for the oracle task; it compiles repository-local `poc/rust` with `--locked` (the lockfile has no third-party crates) and never ships Rust in the Zig artifact. Normal `zig build test` remains Cargo-free.
operationalConsiderations.crossRuntimeContracts: Patch 6 creates one deliberate test-only boundary: the Zig CLI and frozen Rust CLI receive the same source corpus. Successful cases compare exit status and canonical stdout byte-for-byte; failure cases compare the semantic kind/word fields while ignoring source positions, traces, and wording that are implementation-contextual. A checked manifest maps every shared M5 word to at least one case, so adding or omitting a shared word fails the harness. `flip`, `reshape`, and `group` are Zig-only acceptance fixtures because changing the frozen oracle to add them would destroy its role.
operationalConsiderations.failureBehavior: All allocation failures continue as `error.OutOfMemory`; no kernel converts OOM into a language error or panic. Language faults are ordinary d.19 errors: type/domain/shape/conform, checked overflow, division by zero, NaN production, non-finite-from-finite results, and a 256-level pervasion depth guard. Checked leaf loops stage one 256-element block, test its fault mask before any aliased store, rescan only the failing block to report zero-based `data.index`, and rely on unit rollback to discard all partial fresh output. Shape products use checked multiplication; empty data may reshape only to an exactly representable zero-volume nested-list shape, whose zero dimension is final; malformed format strings and placeholder-count mismatches retain the Rust oracle's domain/contract distinction.
operationalConsiderations.concurrencyAndIdempotency: Kernels remain single-threaded and own no workers. Every low-level loop accepts an explicit half-open `IndexRange`, and top-level loops call `Machine.pollKernel` after each 65,536 logical elements; this is the M7 cancellation seam and makes retry/discard safe because values are immutable outside an rc==1 buffer owned by the current primitive. CoW reuse is deterministic: consume owned operands, prefer a unique width-compatible left header, then right, otherwise allocate; shared headers are never mutated. Atomic RC publication/uniqueness orderings remain unchanged and TSan-covered.
operationalConsiderations.rollbackStrategy: There are no migrations or persistent external writes. Any patch can be reverted with ordinary source control; words added by that patch simply cease to be core bindings. At runtime, failures use the existing transactional-unit checkpoint: a failed kernel cannot publish its result to the data stack, and mask-before-store preserves a stolen input block until its fault has been ruled out.

functionalChanges.description: All pervasive arithmetic, comparison, and logic words are live over atoms and leaves: + - * / div mod pow min max, = <> < > <= >=, and/or, neg/abs/sqrt/floor/ceil/round/not, with exact mixed-number comparison, d.22 float behavior, and d.15 char arithmetic.

Pervasion follows d.13 through ragged generic spines with atom extension, pairwise leading-axis conformability, a depth guard, and dict-value/key-aligned union semantics; leaf and spine paths produce the same logical value and printed representation.

Checked leaf kernels batch faults without losing language precision: a fault reports the first zero-based leaf index, unique width-compatible inputs may be reused only after mask-before-store, shared inputs remain immutable, and long loops poll at bounded chunks.

The structural/search vocabulary is live over specialized leaves and generic spines: at (including nested index vectors and whole-value composite dict keys), where, in, find, raze, cat, take, drop, reverse, first, rest, range, shape, and len preserve zero-length strings, codepoints, and construction-specialization semantics.

The new `flip` and `reshape` words are live: flip transposes the first two axes of rectangular data (rank-one is identity) when the transposed shape remains exactly representable, while reshape validates a non-empty non-negative shape, checks its product, ravels input row-major, and cycles it; zero-volume results are accepted exactly when no axis follows a zero, because nested lists have no hidden rank metadata for retaining later axes.

`grade` returns a stable ascending permutation and `sort` produces the corresponding stable value order, using comparison for small/generic inputs and range-adaptive bucket/LSD-radix paths for i64, f64, and char leaves without changing numeric ordering (including -0.0 = 0.0).

`distinct` keeps first occurrences and `group` returns an insertion-ordered dict from each distinct value to its stable index vector, using poll-aware structural hash buckets with equality checks for collisions rather than quadratic full scans.

The dict vocabulary is live with immutable insertion-order semantics: keys, vals, put, del, merge (right wins), and has?; has? performs a whole-value lookup for every legal structural key, and unique dict headers may adopt replacements while shared dictionaries are unchanged.

The string vocabulary is live over Unicode codepoints: split performs substring splitting (including the oracle's empty-separator behavior), join requires a list of strings, and format implements positional `{}` placeholders plus `{{`/`}}` escapes using canonical rendering and domain/contract failures.

SourceHut blocks on a cross-implementation corpus covering every M5 word shared with the frozen Rust PoC, including canonical str, while normal Zig tests remain independent of the Rust toolchain; post-freeze Zig-only behavior is locked by native tests and the real-binary array-words fixture.
`cmp` returns -1/0/1 whole-value ordering (numbers exact, chars, strings lexicographic; else 'type) and `grade`/`sort` order by exactly cmp's ordering, including string elements.

`type` returns the value's kind symbol from the closed atom set; `str` returns canonical round-trip source; `put` updates list elements functionally and produces the same specialized representation on unique and shared paths; `to-dict` builds a dict from two conformable lists.
`take` beyond length cycles; `where` replicates indices by counts; `exp log sin cos atan2` compute pervasively with d.22 edge mapping.

contextResources.why: Normative M5 semantics and architecture: d.2/3/4/13/15/16/17/22/23, exact stack effects, the static leaf-loop matrix, pervasion and broadcast, fault-mask licensing, reuse order, stable/range-adaptive grade, hash grouping, chunk polls, line budget, and the M5/M6 ownership boundary.

The frozen tags and actual ownership APIs the kernels must use: Header.kind/setKind, heap raw slices/isUnique/adoptRepresentation, list specialization and borrowed indexing, indexed ordered dicts, exact number comparison, structural equality/hash, and canonical representation-exposing output.

The traced live path and installation lifecycle: CLI -> persistent Session -> machine dispatch -> env.Primitive; Session.initFull calls prims.install and the core seals afterward. Kernel code must plug into this path without changing evaluation frames or late binding.

Executable semantic oracle for all shared words: scalar/pervasive rules, sequence edge behavior, stable comparison grade, dict insertion order, string formatting, CLI output, and exact mixed-number comparisons. Its boxed values, recursive per-element implementation, quadratic distinct, and eager allocation are explicitly disqualified as implementation precedents; it is never edited.

Existing build/test aggregation, real-artifact process harness, SourceHut gates, and dedicated `zig build source-audit` component audit. Patch 1 must keep every ordinary gate green with skipped stubs; Patch 6 extends the graph without making Cargo a normal-test dependency.

NumPy documents the applicable structure: a static list of one-dimensional inner loops selected once for a concrete type signature, with scalar broadcast represented as stride zero rather than materialized data. Patch 1 adopts the dispatch shape; Patch 2 applies it to ecl's fixed leaf tags.

Pinned Zig 0.16 documentation for comptime-known @Vector elementwise operations, scalar fallback on unsupported targets, and explicit overflow/wrapping primitives. The implementation must remain valid in Debug, ReleaseSafe, ReleaseFast, and Linux TSan.

Concrete array-language precedent for stable grade, small insertion/comparison paths, small-range bucket methods, and stable LSD radix above roughly 100 elements. ecl adds signed/float key transforms and preserves its own exact numeric ordering.

Array-language treatment of mask-to-indices and bucket-prefix construction informs `where` and the counting/group paths without importing BQN's packed-boolean representation, which ecl has explicitly deferred.

acceptanceCriteria: All ordinary gates remain green: `zig fmt --check .`, `zig build test`, ReleaseSafe, ReleaseFast, named TSan, and ZLint --deny-warnings; SourceHut additionally runs the Cargo-backed oracle task.

The shared dispatch artifact uses `value.HeapKind` directly (no second leaf-tag enum): unary selection is (op, tag), binary selection is (op, left tag, right tag), invalid combinations are explicit null/error entries, and a structural test proves selection happens once per flat operation rather than per element.

Every leaf or structural traversal polls after at most 65,536 logical elements, including list/dict update copies and values nested beneath distinct/group inputs; kernels create no threads and make no scheduler decisions.
DoD-3/4: `[[1 2] [3]] 10 *` prints `([10 20] [30])`; `[1 2] [1 2] =` prints `[1 1]`; whole-value `match` still prints `1`; list/list mismatches raise 'conform with both leading-axis lengths.

DoD-5: `9223372036854775806 [1 2] +` raises 'overflow with `'word '+` and `data.index = 1`; tests hit the first, last, and cross-block positions and prove a unique stolen input is unchanged through the failing block.

DoD-6/16: inf operands propagate, `inf inf -` is 'domain, finite-to-inf is 'overflow, division by ±0 is 'domain, floor/ceil/round return int64 or 'overflow, exact comparisons remain correct above 2^53, and `\a 1 +` is `\b`; scalar and leaf paths agree.

All structural/search words in FC-4 work over each relevant representation, including Unicode-codepoint string indexing, nested index-vector gather, whole-value dict lookup for composite keys, non-negative count-vector replication (with masks as the 0/1 case), first-match-or-len find, negative take/drop from the end, zero-length string preservation, and specialization after raze/cat/reverse/rest/put regardless of reference count.

`shape` returns the full rectangular shape and raises 'shape on ragged data. `flip` transposes the first two axes and preserves deeper cells; rank-one input is unchanged, and a transpose that would put zero before a later axis raises 'shape rather than collapsing rank. `reshape` rejects empty/rank-zero shape vectors and negative/overflowing dimensions, ravels input row-major, cycles it, permits empty input for zero-volume output when the zero dimension is final, and rejects unrepresentable later axes rather than returning a value with a false shape.
DoD-17's `array-words.ecl` stdout matches `array-words.out` exactly: flip, 2x3 reshape, group insertion order, and `[2 1 2 1] grade` -> `[1 3 0 2]`.

Grade is stable on every path. Tests force the small comparison, small-range bucket, signed i64 radix, char-width, f64 bit-flip, and generic mixed-number paths; -0.0/0.0 retain input order, infinities sort at the ends, and NaN is never admitted.

Distinct/group use poll-aware structural hashes plus equality collision checks and preserve first occurrence order; an injected same-hash fixture proves collisions do not merge unequal values, and a nested value larger than 65,536 cells proves cancellation charging descends through structure. Dict merge is indexed/right-wins and preserves the left position of replaced keys followed by new right keys.

Split/join/format match the frozen oracle on ASCII and Unicode fixtures, empty separators, escaped braces, malformed braces, non-string join members, and too many/few placeholders; resulting strings use the narrowest char leaf.

The oracle manifest covers every shared M5 word at least once and rejects duplicate/missing coverage. Successful cases compare canonical stdout exactly; error cases compare exit status plus semantic kind/word. `poc/rust` has no diff after the milestone.
Every kernel family has a `std.testing.checkAllAllocationFailures` probe, and the full tree remains leak-free under `std.testing.allocator`.

`zig build source-audit` reports kernels <= 5,500 lines and continues to enforce each existing core component and the 9,500-line total independently; moving scalar primitives out of prims leaves the machine at or below 2,300 lines.

`cmp` fixtures: `9223372036854775807 -9223372036854775808 cmp` is 1 (where `-` would overflow); `9007199254740993 9007199254740992.0 cmp` is 1 (exactness); `"apple" "apricot" cmp` is -1; `'a 'b cmp` and `1 "x" cmp` are 'type; `["b" "a"] grade` is `[1 0]` — grade/cmp agreement locked by a shared fixture table.

Supplemental vocabulary fixtures: `3.5 type` is 'float and case-dispatch on type works; `['a 1] str` is canonical re-readable source and agrees with the frozen oracle; `[1 2 3] 1 9 put` is `[1 9 3]`; `['a 'b] [1 2] to-dict` matches `{'a 1 'b 2}`; `[1 2] 5 take` is `[1 2 1 2 1]`; `[2 0 3] where` is `[0 0 2 2 2]`; `0 log` is 'overflow and `-1 log` is 'domain; the oracle differential job documents the post-freeze exclusions.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Reuse `value.HeapKind`; do not create a kernel-local leaf enum.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The M1 tag set was frozen specifically to be shared by storage, printing, and dispatch. A second enum would require translation and allow symbol/reserved-mask drift.

explicitOpinions.opinion: Kernel entry consumes its operands and returns one owned result.
explicitOpinions.rationale: This maps directly to the stack's ownership-passing discipline and makes CoW unambiguous: a reused header transfers into the result, unused operands are released exactly once, and no caller performs pointer-identity release dances.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The pervasion host-stack guard is 256 list/dict levels.
explicitOpinions.rationale: Evaluation remains non-recursive, but data descent is explicitly allowed on the host stack only behind a guard. 256 is far beyond practical array rank while giving a fixed safety margin independent of host stack size; exceeding it is a deterministic 'domain error rather than a crash.

explicitOpinions.opinion: `reshape` uses row-major ravel-and-cycle, requires at least one shape dimension, treats a dict as an atomic ravel cell, and rejects a shape with any axis after a zero dimension.
explicitOpinions.rationale: This is the K/APL interpretation of cycling data within ecl's nested-list value model. Because lists carry no hidden rank metadata, `[0 3]` and `[0]` would otherwise produce the same empty value; rejecting the unrepresentable former preserves the stronger invariant that successful `shape reshape` reports the requested shape.

explicitOpinions.opinion: `cmp`, grade, and sort share one deliberately partial order: exact numbers, chars by codepoint, and strings codepoint-lexicographically; every other value or cross-domain pair is a type error.
explicitOpinions.rationale: This makes the whole-value comparator the single semantic order used by grade while refusing to turn intern ids or arbitrary structure into language ordering. Generic spines support mixed numeric leaves and lists of strings, but do not imply a total order over every Value.

explicitOpinions.opinion: `sort` is an honest stored core body; `has?` is primitive key membership; `find` remains provisional direct until M6.
explicitOpinions.rationale: `sort = (dup grade at)` preserves the [E] proof and `body` honesty. `has?` is deliberately not defined as attempted lookup: it performs a native membership probe so every Value is inert, only absence becomes false, and cancellation/allocation failures propagate. VOCABULARY's find definition depends on `each`, which M6 owns; a temporary direct find kernel gives M5 its promised search surface without prematurely implementing combinator semantics or adding a shadow compiled form.

explicitOpinions.opinion: The Rust oracle job is separate from ordinary Zig tests.
explicitOpinions.rationale: The PoC is valuable as a semantic cross-check but is not a shipped dependency. Developers and downstream packagers can test/build the real interpreter with only pinned Zig; CI pays the extra Cargo cost once.

explicitOpinions.opinion: M5 does not add M6's fused-vs-generic harness or idiom table.
explicitOpinions.rationale: M5 proves leaf kernels against their spine path and the frozen oracle. M6 owns quotation recognition, resolution-identity guards, and the named fast-vs-frame-machine differential harness; pulling those forward would duplicate the exact soundness boundary the workstream separated.

changes: Define `Context` around *Machine, with allocator, fail, failAtIndex, conform, and poll helpers; top-level family functions consume owned Values and return one owned Value or release everything on error.
Define BinaryOp/UnaryOp/SequenceOp/OrderOp once in kernel_support and generate uniform primitive adapters with comptime parameters; low-level leaf loops always receive IndexRange.

Move the existing M3 scalar arithmetic/comparison and scalar list `at` implementations byte-for-semantics behind kernel family install functions, so Patch 1 changes no CLI outcome and frees prims.zig budget.

Add `Machine.pollKernel`: increment the poll counter and check the cancellation flag on every call; the unit-wide kernel fuel polls before a bounded block that reaches the boundary and charges that whole block to the fresh interval. Add error data keys index/left/right and helpers without changing existing error dicts.
Install skipped tests with `return error.SkipZigTest`; all ordinary tests and all optimization modes stay green while naming every later proof up front.
Audit kernel production files separately from core and count all four kernel test files as tests only.

patches.title: Implement checked leaf arithmetic and recursive d.13 pervasion

files.description: Full numeric/logic matrix, pervasive descent, dict alignment, fault blocks, char/float semantics, and reuse.
Implement and unskip every numeric proof from Patch 1.

changes: Install the closed binary family (+ - * / div mod pow min max = <> < > <= >= and or) and unary family (neg abs sqrt floor ceil round not) through comptime-bound primitive functions.

Build unary (op, HeapKind) and binary (op, left HeapKind, right HeapKind) tables. Normalize char widths at entry, handle leaf/leaf and leaf/scalar without per-element Value/tag dispatch, and return an explicit type error for null matrix entries.

Implement leading-axis recursion: list/list length check then pairwise descent, atom/list extension, scalar atoms at the bottom, output reconstructed through poll-aware specialized storage constructors, and a 256-level domain guard.

Implement dict unary/scalar pervasion over values and dict/dict alignment as left-order union: matching keys recurse, unmatched left and right values pass through unchanged, new right keys append in right order.

Use 256-element staged blocks and fixed small @Vector lanes where the operation supports them; fault masks cover integer overflow, invalid bools, division/modulo by zero, invalid Unicode results, NaN, and finite-to-infinite results. On a fault, rescan the untouched block and call failAtIndex for the first lane.

Apply the left-unique then right-unique then fresh reuse order for width-compatible outputs; preserve shared inputs and specialize fresh/generic results identically. Mixed min/max that must preserve the selected atom type use a generic Value spine rather than silently promoting.
Call pollKernel after each 65,536 logical leaf elements and exhaust allocator failures through scalar, leaf, spine, and dict paths.

---
> Atoms extend over lists; two lists descend pairwise when their leading
> axes conform.
all o: BinaryOp, a: Value, b: Value, scalar? a, list? b |
  length (result-value (pervade o a b)) = length b.
all o: BinaryOp, a: Value, b: Value, list? a, list? b, length a = length b, i: Index |
  element (result-value (pervade o a b)) i =
    result-value (pervade o (element a i) (element b i)).

> Dicts preserve the union of keys; matching values recurse and unmatched
> values are identities.
all o: BinaryOp, a: Value, b: Value, dict? a, dict? b, k: Key, has-key? a k, has-key? b k |
  dict-value (result-value (pervade o a b)) k =
    result-value (pervade o (dict-value a k) (dict-value b k)).
all o: BinaryOp, a: Value, b: Value, dict? a, dict? b, k: Key, has-key? a k, has-key? b k = false |
  dict-value (result-value (pervade o a b)) k = dict-value a k.

> Batched execution still reports the first logical fault.
all o: BinaryOp, a: Value, b: Value, faults? o a b |
  apply-binary o a b = overflow (first-fault o a b).

patches.title: Implement cmp, stable grade/sort, and hash distinct/group

files.description: All ordering, distinct, and group algorithms plus bindings and stored sort body.
Implement and unskip every ordering proof from Patch 1.

changes: Install `cmp` ( x y -- n ): three-way whole-value ordering returning -1/0/1, NOT pervasive — cmp is to < what match is to = (ruled 2026-08-12, VOCABULARY.md). Domain: numbers via the exact mixed int/float ordering equal.compareScalars already implements, chars by codepoint, strings codepoint-lexicographic; every other operand or cross-kind pair is 'type. cmp and grade must agree: grade's comparator IS cmp's order extended element-wise, so string elements grade lexicographically.
Install grade, distinct, and group primitives. Install sort as the real stored core body `(dup grade at)`, not a second primitive or cached form.

Grade produces i64 indices and is stable on all routes: stable insertion/comparison for small and generic mixed-number spines; min/max range probe then stable bucket placement for small-range i64/chars; stable LSD radix for larger i64/char/f64 leaves with constant high bytes skipped.

Transform signed i64 keys by flipping the sign bit. Transform f64 keys by canonicalizing both zero signs before the standard sign-aware bit flip; NaN is rejected defensively even though readers/kernels never create it; infinities sort naturally.
Sort uses the stored grade+at semantics in M5; no idiom recognition lands before M6. Tests assert its value and representation equal an explicit grade/gather.

Distinct/group hash with equal.hashWithPolling, retain a collision chain per hash, and use equal.matchWithPolling before coalescing. Polling follows every nested list/dict value rather than charging only the outer cell. Distinct keeps the first Value; group uses that Value as the dict key and appends stable i64 indices.
Force every algorithm branch in tests, include adversarial equal-key stability and hash-collision fixtures, poll long passes, and sweep OOM.

---
> Cmp is the partial whole-value order consumed by grade.
all a: Value, b: Value, comparable? a b, less? a b | cmp a b = cmp-less.
all a: Value, b: Value, comparable? a b, equal? a b | cmp a b = cmp-equal.
all a: Value, b: Value, comparable? a b, greater? a b | cmp a b = cmp-greater.
all a: Value, b: Value, comparable? a b = false | cmp a b = cmp-type-error.

> Comparability is symmetric; cmp is reflexive at equality and
> antisymmetric at less/greater throughout its domain.
all a: Value, b: Value, comparable? a b | comparable? b a.
all a: Value, comparable? a a | cmp a a = cmp-equal.
all a: Value, b: Value, comparable? a b, cmp a b = cmp-less | cmp b a = cmp-greater.
all a: Value, b: Value, comparable? a b | sorts-before? a b = (cmp a b = cmp-less).
all a: Value, b: Value, comparable? a b | less? a b = sorts-before? a b.

> Sort is exactly grade followed by gather.
all s: Sequence | sort s = at s (grade s).
all s: Sequence | permutation-count (grade s) = count s.

> Grade is ascending and stable for equal values.
all s: Sequence, i: Nat0, j: Nat0, i < count s, j < count s, i < j |
  sorts-before? (value s (source-index (grade s) j))
        (value s (source-index (grade s) i)) = false.
all s: Sequence, i: Nat0, j: Nat0, i < count s, j < count s, i < j, equal? (value s i) (value s j) |
  rank-of (grade s) i < rank-of (grade s) j.

> Distinct retains exactly the first-seen equivalence classes; group maps
> each input value to a stable index sequence containing its position.
all s: Sequence | first-occurrences? (distinct s) s.
all s: Sequence, i: Nat0, i < count s | group-has? (group s) (value s i).
all s: Sequence, i: Nat0, i < count s |
  contains-index? (group-indices (group s) (value s i)) i.

---
> Leading-axis pervasion and scalar extension.
all op: BinaryOp, left: Value, right: Value, scalar? left, list? right |
  length (result-value (pervade op left right)) = length right.
all op: BinaryOp, left: Value, right: Value, list? left, list? right, length left = length right, index: Nat0 |
  element (result-value (pervade op left right)) index =
    result-value (pervade op (element left index) (element right index)).

> Dict alignment combines matches and preserves unmatched left values.
all op: BinaryOp, left: Value, right: Value, dict? left, dict? right, key: Key, has-key? left key, has-key? right key |
  dict-value (result-value (pervade op left right)) key =
    result-value (pervade op (dict-value left key) (dict-value right key)).
all op: BinaryOp, left: Value, right: Value, dict? left, dict? right, key: Key, has-key? left key, has-key? right key = false |
  dict-value (result-value (pervade op left right)) key = dict-value left key.

> Rectangular shape succeeds; flip swaps only the first two axes; reshape
> has exactly the requested representable non-empty shape.
all val: Value, rectangular? val |
  shape-of val = shape-result (result-shape (shape-of val)).
all val: Value, rectangular? val = false | shape-of val = shape-error.
all val: Value, rectangular? val, flip-representable? val |
  result-shape (flip val) = swapped-leading (result-shape (shape-of val)).
all val: Value, rectangular? val, flip-representable? val = false | flip val = shape-error.
all shape: Shape, rank shape <= 1 | swapped-leading shape = shape.
all shape: Shape, rank shape > 1 | axis (swapped-leading shape) 0 = axis shape 1.
all shape: Shape, rank shape > 1 | axis (swapped-leading shape) 1 = axis shape 0.
all shape: Shape, rank shape > 1, index: Nat0, index >= 2 |
  axis (swapped-leading shape) index = axis shape index.
all val: Value, shape: Shape, rank shape > 0, volume shape = 0, representable? shape |
  result-shape (reshape val shape) = shape.
all val: Value, shape: Shape, rank shape > 0, representable? shape = false |
  reshape val shape = shape-error.

> Cmp is the partial whole-value order consumed by grade.
all left: Value, right: Value, comparable? left right, less? left right | cmp left right = cmp-less.
all left: Value, right: Value, comparable? left right, equal? left right | cmp left right = cmp-equal.
all left: Value, right: Value, comparable? left right, greater? left right | cmp left right = cmp-greater.
all left: Value, right: Value, comparable? left right = false | cmp left right = cmp-type-error.

> Comparability is symmetric; cmp is reflexive at equality and
> antisymmetric at less/greater throughout its domain.
all left: Value, right: Value, comparable? left right | comparable? right left.
all val: Value, comparable? val val | cmp val val = cmp-equal.
all left: Value, right: Value, comparable? left right, cmp left right = cmp-less | cmp right left = cmp-greater.
all left: Value, right: Value, comparable? left right | sorts-before? left right = (cmp left right = cmp-less).
all left: Value, right: Value, comparable? left right | less? left right = sorts-before? left right.

> Ordering is grade/gather, ascending, and stable.
all seq: Sequence | sort seq = at seq (grade seq).
all seq: Sequence | permutation-count (grade seq) = count seq.
all seq: Sequence, i: Nat0, j: Nat0, i < count seq, j < count seq, i < j |
  sorts-before? (value seq (source-index (grade seq) j))
        (value seq (source-index (grade seq) i)) = false.
all seq: Sequence, i: Nat0, j: Nat0, i < count seq, j < count seq, i < j, equal? (value seq i) (value seq j) |
  rank-of (grade seq) i < rank-of (grade seq) j.
all seq: Sequence | first-occurrences? (distinct seq) seq.
all seq: Sequence, index: Nat0, index < count seq |
  group-has? (group seq) (value seq index).
all seq: Sequence, index: Nat0, index < count seq |
  contains-index? (group-indices (group seq) (value seq index)) index.

> Dict updates are functional and right-biased.
all dict: Dict, key: Key, val: Value | lookup (put dict key val) key = val.
all dict: Dict, key: Key | contains-key? (del dict key) key = false.
all dict: Dict, other-dict: Dict, key: Key, contains-key? other-dict key |
  lookup (merge dict other-dict) key = lookup other-dict key.

> Split and join round-trip separator-free members.
all parts: StringList, separator: String, nonempty? separator, separator-free? parts separator |
  join (split (join parts separator) separator) separator = join parts separator.

> Supplemental kind, collection, cycling, replicate, and transcendental rules.
all val: Value | kind val = int-k or kind val = float-k or kind val = char-k or kind val = symbol-k or kind val = word-k or kind val = list-k or kind val = dict-k.
all val: Value | read-back (render val) = val.
all items: ArrayList, index: Nat0, val: Value, index < list-count items | list-nth (put-at items index val) index = val.
all items: ArrayList, index: Nat0, val: Value, other: Nat0, index < list-count items, other < list-count items, ~(other = index) | list-nth (put-at items index val) other = list-nth items other.
all items: ArrayList, index: Nat0, val: Value, index < list-count items | list-count (put-at items index val) = list-count items.
> take-count-correct? abstracts list-count (take-n items amount) = amount
> because Pantagruel's bounded opaque domains cannot realize every Nat0 length.
all items: ArrayList, amount: Nat0 | take-count-correct? items amount.
all items: ArrayList, index: Nat0, index < list-count items | cyclic items index = list-nth items index.
all items: ArrayList, index: Nat0, list-count items > 0 | cyclic items (index + list-count items) = cyclic items index.
all items: ArrayList | list-count (where-counts items) = replicate-total items.
all keys: ArrayList, vals: ArrayList, distinct-keys? keys, list-count keys = list-count vals | keys-of (to-dict keys vals) = keys.
all keys: ArrayList, vals: ArrayList, distinct-keys? keys, list-count keys = list-count vals | vals-of (to-dict keys vals) = vals.
all operation: Op, val: Value, would-be-nan1? operation val | apply1 operation val = err-domain.
all operation: Op, left: Value, right: Value, would-be-nan2? operation left right | apply2 operation left right = err-domain.
all operation: Op, val: Value, nonfinite-from-finite1? operation val | apply1 operation val = err-overflow.
all operation: Op, left: Value, right: Value, nonfinite-from-finite2? operation left right | apply2 operation left right = err-overflow.

> The oracle boundary is exhaustive; new Zig-only words have their own
> executable assertion.
all word: SharedWord | covered? word.
all word: SharedWord | agrees? word.
verified? array-words.
